title: Per Diem Grace Days After Buyer Closing Extensions, by Home Purchase Agreement Collection
content:
On a Home Purchase Agreement, the grace days of a closing delay period shrink once the buyer has asked to extend the closing. The count is of closing extension fee charges on the agreement ledger, whatever their dates:

- where the ledger carries **two or more** closing extension fee charges, the period has no grace days;
- where it carries **exactly one**, the period's grace days are one day fewer than the collection's per diem grace days, never fewer than zero;
- where it carries none, the grace days are not reduced.

## Schedule of grace days

| Collection | Per diem grace days of the collection | Grace days with exactly one closing extension fee charge | Grace days with two or more closing extension fee charges |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pathway Collection | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Meadow Collection | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Heritage Collection | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Crestview Collection | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Summit Collection | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| Reserve Collection | 2 | 1 | 0 |

## Notes to the schedule

1. In the Pathway and Meadow Collections the collection figure is 0, so one fewer is held at zero.
2. A Summit Collection or Reserve Collection agreement whose ledger shows one closing extension fee charge has 1 grace day; with a second such charge it has none.
3. *Hypothetical illustration.* A Heritage Collection agreement whose ledger shows one closing extension fee charge, from an extension requested before the scheduled closing date, has 0 grace days in its delay period; with no closing extension fee charge it keeps its 1 grace day.
